name: versus
title: Versus
description: Two sides, head to head: each side's player or team, each side's score as a `stat`, and a bar splitting the two by share. A side that is a player is an `identity` and a side that is a team is a name, because a team has no avatar case and no presence: every side carries `data-gs-side`, then `data-gs-player` or `data-gs-team` depending on what it stands for, and the player's side never also carries `data-gs-you`. The outcome is `data-gs-outcome` with a mark beside the score and the past-tense word in the accessible name, so who won never rests on the colour. The share is a custom property rather than an attribute, the same decision `progress-bar` made: there is no `data-gs-progress` and no `data-gs-fill`. Performs nothing: the host owns both numbers and decides who won.
docs: Pass `player` and `opponent`, each with a score and either a `player` from the adapter or a `team` id with a `label`. Two sides and never three: a board of many is `leaderboard`. Set `outcome` on each side once you know how it finished; the component never decides it, and the two sides are independent, so a forfeit can be a loss without the other side being a win. Pass `split={false}` where the two numbers are not a whole that can be divided, a lap time against a lap time for instance: the bar would otherwise read as a share of something that does not exist. Two zero scores render as half each rather than dividing by nought, and a negative score is clamped to the track. Read `data-gs-value` on each side's stat for the numbers, never the rendered text.
